You look at the restrictions on Bea’s loan record.

“Could one of the photographs be displayed for the reopening?”

“Not under this agreement,” Nell says at once.

She turns the page so the relevant clause sits between you. Public display, publication and scanning all require further written permission from Bea.

“And that permission would need to identify the particular photograph and its intended use. We couldn’t treat approval for one image as approval for the album.”

Nell closes the folder but keeps her hand on it.

“Bea wants to speak to the people pictured before she agrees to public use. Some photographs are staff events; others are private family occasions away from the cinema. She hasn’t begun those conversations, and we’re not turning the reopening deadline into pressure on her.”

The album remains in the locked cupboard across the room.

“Even with Bea’s agreement, we would still check who took the photograph, whether any copyright information survives and what caption or context we intended to provide. Owning the album doesn’t answer all of that.”

She returns the loan record to its sleeve.

“Your inventory can describe each photograph without reproducing it. Approximate date, setting, people who are reliably identified, physical condition and anything written on the back—provided the photograph can be examined without forcing or dismantling the album. If something looks potentially useful for future interpretation, mark a catalogue query. Don’t remove it or promise it to an exhibition.”

Nell carries the folder back to its shelf.

“Rosa hasn’t requested pictures from this album. Her reopening display is based on the programme boards, and it can proceed without anything you catalogue. So for the twenty-sixth, the answer is no unless Bea independently completes those conversations and signs a further agreement. We plan on the basis that she won’t.”

The cupboard stays locked. No photograph is taken out, copied or shown. Nell returns to the trust-owned business papers on the table and continues the induction.
